description: Temporary, expiring acceptances for reviewed Expo developer-tooling advisories. node-forge has no upstream release outside its advisory range, and zod 3 (the only line @expo/cli accepts) has none either. None of these paths accepts approval traffic, and each entry must be removed when its stated remediation becomes eligible.

exceptions.title: Zod can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections
exceptions.reachability: Developer-machine CLI tooling only. The single installed zod 3.25.76 copy is reached through expo -> @expo/cli 57.0.27 -> zod (declared ^3.25.76). Reviewed from the lockfile and npm explain on 2026-10-26: no other package in this app's tree depends on zod, and the installed copy is marked as a dependency of @expo/cli only. This entry makes no claim about which inputs @expo/cli validates with zod; the exposure is a memory-exhausting input to a local Expo CLI run, not device-reachable application code.

no_upstream_fix.how_checked: zod 4.6.6 (2026-10-11) and 4.6.7 (2026-10-12) are outside the advisory range, but @expo/cli 57.0.27 declares zod ^3.25.76, so a major-version override would swap the CLI's validation library for a release line it was not built against.
no_upstream_fix.why_suggested_fix_rejected: Overriding @expo/cli's zod 3 dependency to 4.x risks breaking the Expo CLI's own schema validation and is not something the CLI's maintainers support.

exceptions.revisit_trigger: When @expo/cli ships a release that accepts zod >=4.6.6, refresh the lock, require a zero-advisory npm audit, and delete this entry. Revisit immediately if any app source imports zod, if npm reports a new package in this advisory's affected set, or if severity changes.

exceptions.title: deepmerge mergeObject() allows prototype poisoning of returned objects
exceptions.reachability: Developer and CI build tooling only. The single installed copy is deepmerge 4.3.1, reached through expo 57.0.31 into @expo/cli, @expo/config, @expo/metro-config, @expo/prebuild-config and @expo/local-build-cache-provider (verified with npm ls on 2026-10-27). These packages merge developer-authored app, Metro and prebuild configuration on the developer or CI machine. Nothing derived from approval requests, pairing payloads, receipts or network input reaches mergeObject, and the merged configuration is not shipped in the device bundle.

no_upstream_fix.how_checked: GitHub advisory GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 lists no first patched version. npm view deepmerge version returns 4.3.1, which is inside the vulnerable range.
no_upstream_fix.why_suggested_fix_rejected: expo 51 is a major SDK behind the pinned expo 57.0.31, which would trade one low-severity build-time advisory for an unsupported runtime.

exceptions.revisit_trigger: When deepmerge publishes a release outside >=4.2.0 <=4.3.1, refresh the lock so @expo/config resolves it, require a zero-advisory npm audit, and delete this entry. Revisit immediately if the Expo SDK upgrades and deepmerge leaves the tree, or if @expo/config starts merging untrusted input.
